title: MLflow React development UI fails locally because API requests are not reaching the backend
body: I am developing MLflow from source on an M1 Mac with MLflow 2.20.4.dev0, Python 3.9.20, Node v22.14.0, and Yarn 1.22.22. I created and activated the development environment, ran `mlflow ui`, then ran `yarn install` and `yarn start` from `mlflow/server/js`. Opening `http://localhost:3000/` shows request errors instead of the MLflow UI. I changed the setup script from `tensorflow-cpu<=2.12.0` to `tensorflow-macos<=2.12.0` for the Arm Mac.

symptoms_visible: When I open http://localhost:3000/, the page shows 'A request error occurred.: undefined' and '[object Object]' runtime errors instead of the MLflow UI.
N0.label: N0 React development UI request error

symptoms_visible: The MLflow UI opens normally at http://127.0.0.1:5000, but my frontend code changes do not hot-reload there.
The development page on port 3000 still shows errors, and its experiment-search request returns 404.
N1.label: N1 direct UI works but development request fails

symptoms_visible: The request to http://localhost:3000/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/search?max_results=20000 returns an empty 404 response with both Express and AirTunes-related headers.
The MLflow server terminal only shows normal Gunicorn startup and worker messages.
N2.label: N2 response and process evidence collected

symptoms_visible: After deleting node_modules and reinstalling the JavaScript dependencies, the development UI still shows the same request error and the API request still returns 404.
N2_x.label: N2_x dependency reinstall aftermath

symptoms_visible: The browser still reports the failed experiment-search request, while the yarn terminal says webpack compiled with warnings, files were emitted, and no type-check issues were found.
No new proxy or connection error appears in the yarn terminal when the browser request fails.
N3.label: N3 frontend build succeeds without proxy diagnostics

symptoms_visible: After running yarn build and opening the UI through the MLflow server, I still get a 404 error.
N3_x.label: N3_x production build workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: The same 404 and frontend request errors remain after downgrading Node to v20.15.0.
The browser sends the experiment-search request to the ajax-api path on port 3000.
N4_x.label: N4_x Node downgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: After clearing everything and restarting my computer, the local MLflow development UI works again.
N_terminal.label: terminal local proxy path working after restart

question_patterns: Can you open the UI served by `mlflow ui`, for example at http://127.0.0.1:5000?
Does the page on port 5000 work when you open it without going through the Yarn development page?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, it works on port 5000, but my code changes do not appear there, so I still need to know how to use hot reload.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, port 5000 is also unreachable and `mlflow ui` exits with a server error.
The UI works at 127.0.0.1:5000 and localhost:5000, but neither hot-reloads frontend changes.

question_patterns: What does `mlflow.search_experiments(filter_string="name = ''")` return after setting the tracking URI to the server on port 5000?
Can the Python client call the experiment-search API through the direct MLflow server?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I set the tracking URI to http://127.0.0.1:5000 and `mlflow.search_experiments(filter_string="name = ''")` returns an empty list.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Python call also returns 403 or 404 from the server on port 5000.

question_patterns: What status do you see for the experiment-search request in the browser developer tools?
Can you share the failing request URL and its response status?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The page still fails, and http://127.0.0.1:3000/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/search?max_results=20000 returns 404 Not Found.

edges.comment: Reporter c1, c3, and c5: the directly served UI and Python request against port 5000 work, while the React development server's ajax-api request returns 404. The image is the reporter's c3 browser evidence.

question_patterns: What is the complete response, including headers, for the failing search-experiments request?
Can you copy the status and response headers from the browser network panel?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found` with `X-Powered-By: Express`, an empty body, and `server: AirTunes/845.5.1`, plus Apple processing headers.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The response is a JSON MLflow error from Gunicorn and has no Express or AirTunes headers.
It is still an empty 404 with Express and AirTunes headers, but the AirTunes build number is slightly different.

question_patterns: Do you see a traceback or request error in the terminal running `mlflow ui`?
What does the MLflow server terminal print when the browser request fails?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I don't think there is another stack trace. It only shows Gunicorn listening at http://127.0.0.1:5000 with four workers booting.

question_patterns: Have you set any MLflow-related proxy or static-proxy environment variables?
Are there custom environment variables affecting the development server?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I did not set `MLFLOW_PROXY` or `MLFLOW_STATIC_PROXY`; they were not in the contributing instructions I followed.

edges.comment: Reporter c7, c9, and c14: raw headers identify an AirTunes-speaking local service in the failed path, while the MLflow Gunicorn process is healthy and no MLflow proxy variables were configured. The causal interpretation remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as a damaged JavaScript dependency installation by deleting the frontend dependency cache and reinstalling it.
solution.concrete_example: Remove `mlflow/server/js/node_modules`, clear the relevant package cache, run `yarn install` again, and restart `yarn start`.

edges.comment: Maintainer c8 and reporter c9: the reporter deleted node_modules and reinstalled the JavaScript packages, but the same 404 remained.

question_patterns: What appears in the terminal running `yarn start` after you reproduce the browser error?
Does the frontend terminal show compilation failures or only warnings?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It shows source-map warnings from ag-grid packages, then says webpack compiled with 10 warnings, files were emitted, and no type-check issues were found.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Webpack fails to compile because setupProxy.js has a syntax error, so the development server never starts.

question_patterns: After reproducing the browser error, does the `yarn start` terminal print any new connection or proxy error?
Do you see an ECONNREFUSED or similar request-proxy message in the frontend terminal?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Not really. After reproducing it I only see the successful webpack and type-check messages plus a Node deprecation warning.

edges.comment: Reporter c14, c16, and c18: the frontend compiles, but reproducing the browser failure emits no useful proxy error. The two c16 screenshots are attached to the terminal/browser evidence requested by the maintainer.

solution.intent: Use a production frontend build served by `mlflow ui` as a temporary way to view code changes without the React development proxy.
solution.concrete_example: Run `yarn build`, then open the built UI through the MLflow server on port 5000; rebuild after each frontend change.

edges.comment: Maintainer c20 and reporter c21: the static-build workaround was tried, but the reporter still observed a 404.

solution.intent: Test whether the frontend failure is caused by using Node 22 by downgrading to the maintainer's Node 20.15.0 version.
solution.concrete_example: Switch the frontend environment from Node v22.14.0 to v20.15.0, reinstall if necessary, restart both servers, and retry the page.

edges.comment: Maintainer c22 and reporter c23-c24: downgrading to Node v20.15.0 did not change the error. The reporter then supplied the browser screenshot showing the ajax-api request addressed to port 3000.

solution.intent: Treat the frontend URL as correct and eliminate the local process or port conflict that prevents the React development server from proxying API requests to MLflow; restart the local services, or move MLflow and the proxy target together to an unused port.
solution.concrete_example: Requests from the browser should remain on localhost:3000; `yarn start` is responsible for forwarding `/ajax-api` to the MLflow backend. Clear the local state and restart the machine or conflicting services, then verify port 5000 is not occupied by a macOS service before starting MLflow. If it is occupied, use another port consistently for both `mlflow ui -p <unused-port>` and the development proxy target. The reporter recovered after clearing everything and restarting; a later affected macOS user specifically reported ControlCenter occupying port 5000 and succeeded after moving both sides to 5001.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the raw 404 response with `server: AirTunes/845.5.1`, while direct access to MLflow at 127.0.0.1:5000 worked. Inferring that localhost-based proxying reached a different macOS service or stale local process is engineer-side reasoning. A later affected user corroborated this mechanism by identifying macOS ControlCenter on localhost:5000 and successfully moving MLflow and setupProxy.js to 5001; that later user's setup must not be presented as the original reporter's own test.

edges.comment: Reporter c26 confirmed resolution on their own machine only after clearing everything and restarting. The more specific ControlCenter/port-5000 account is from a different affected macOS user in c27 and is used only as corroborating evidence, not misattributed to the reporter.

satisfaction_conditions: Must explain that the browser sending `/ajax-api` requests to localhost:3000 is expected: the React development server should proxy those requests to the MLflow backend rather than the browser calling port 5000 directly.

Must identify the accepted technical direction as a local port or proxy-process conflict on macOS, grounded in the healthy direct backend, the failed proxied request, and the AirTunes response header; it must not claim that ControlCenter was conclusively proven on the original reporter's machine.
Must recommend clearing or stopping the conflicting local service and restarting the development processes, or moving both the MLflow backend and development proxy target to the same unused port.
Must not present dependency reinstallation, a production `yarn build`, or downgrading to Node v20.15.0 as the fix; all were tried without changing the reporter's error.
Must ask the reporter to verify that the port-3000 development UI loads and hot reload works before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Software contributor comfortable with Python environments, Yarn, browser developer tools, and editing setup scripts, but unfamiliar with MLflow's React development proxy architecture.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concise; follows diagnostic instructions, pastes exact commands and headers, shares screenshots, and asks direct questions when the expected port behavior is unclear.
